title: Material Receipt Note (GRN)
context: Material Management › Procure-to-Pay (PO Flow) › Material Receipt Note (GRN)

cards.title: Where the Material Receipt Note sits in procurement and inventory flows
cards.body:
The Material Receipt Note represents step ten in Procure-to-Pay and step eight in Goods Receipt.
It immediately follows the Gate Entry where arriving delivery vehicles are logged by security.
Warehouse storekeepers use this document to officially receive physical stock into company facilities.
It serves as the concluding transaction of procurement and the entry point for warehouse stores.
Accepted materials become usable stock, while rejected items are isolated for return to vendor.
The document closes open purchase orders, indents, and inter-unit transfer challans.
Simultaneously, it generates a valued inward record that feeds the Finance payment flow.
If the item requires inspection, the receipt triggers the quality inspection intimation.
A gate entry linked to another receipt cannot be reused, preventing duplicate stores receipts.
Physical verification against this document ensures company stock matches actual deliveries.
Authorizing the receipt note is the exact operational trigger that increments warehouse stock ledgers.
Without this verified document, accounts payable cannot match supplier bills for payment.
The receipt note serves as the official operational hand-off from logistics transporters to stores staff.
Storekeepers verify that delivery container seals are intact before commencing physical unloading.
This document provides transparent proof of delivery protecting the enterprise against supplier disputes.

cards.title: Mandatory receipt header details, vendor bills, and date validations
cards.body:
Creating a receipt note requires critical commercial headers and source document selections.
The user must specify a document type, reference document source, vendor, and verified location.
The supplier bill number and bill date are compulsory to support downstream payment matching.
A freight type must be selected for all direct receipts and multi-party delivery notes.
Supplier bill dates, challan dates, and transport receipt dates cannot be in the future.
If the vendor bill date is later than the receipt document date, the save is blocked.
Driver and vehicle information must conform to formatting rules when company checks are active.
Duplicate receipt numbers are barred by automated yearly document numbering routines.
Division mapping rules require the finance book to be linked to the active operational unit.
Missing mandatory headers halt saving and highlight the exact field requiring attention.
Vehicle details and transport waybill dates ensure full statutory compliance for logistics audits.
Accurate recording of supplier bill details prevents billing disputes during financial voucher passing.
These header validations prevent unreferenced or unapproved shipments from entering company premises.
Verified logistics data ensures transport liabilities and demurrage fees are allocated appropriately.

cards.title: Accepted quantity formulas, tolerance boundaries, and rate adjustments
cards.body:
Line item quantities follow strict mathematical formulas to maintain inventory accuracy.
Accepted quantity is calculated as received quantity minus rejected and free quantities.
The total line value equals the accepted quantity multiplied by the agreed unit rate.
Received quantities must remain within the positive tolerance allowed by the purchase order.
If accepted quantity exceeds the open balance plus tolerance, the save is rejected.
For raw materials where challan quantities are passed on, unit rates are recalculated.
The adjusted rate equals challan quantity multiplied by rate, divided by accepted quantity.
Conversion factors between purchasing units and inventory units must be positive and non-zero.
Every line item must identify an active warehouse location where stock will be deposited.
These mathematical checks protect the organization against over-billing and stock discrepancies.
Batch tracking details and expiry dates are mandatory for items marked for shelf-life control.
Tolerance rules prevent suppliers from dispatching excess unordered stock into company stores.
Accepted materials are stamped with unique inward batch identifiers to facilitate physical traceability.
Damaged packages are segregated immediately in designated quarantine areas pending formal supplier return.
These strict mathematical calculations guarantee that company accounts reflect verified delivery quantities.

cards.title: Reference combination integrity and currency consistency rules
cards.body:
A single receipt note can combine multiple source references under strict conditions.
All combined purchase orders or gate passes must share the same operational source type.
Combined references must use identical transaction currencies and compatible exchange rates.
Mixing references with conflicting currencies causes the system to stop the transaction.
Only a single inter-unit dispatch challan can be linked to any individual receipt note.
Gate entries already consumed by an existing receipt cannot be selected a second time.
Document dates cannot precede historical cutoff dates established by system configuration.
Tax schedules and consignee locations must align across all selected reference documents.
These consistency rules prevent mismatched financial postings and entangled document lineage.
Users must ensure reference uniformity before allocating received quantities across line items.
Discrepancies in currency or exchange rates halt saving until references are reconciled.
Uniform reference selection ensures clean three-way matching during accounts payable processing.
Storekeepers cannot mix local and imported purchase orders within a single receipt note document.
These consistency rules prevent administrative confusion and preserve transparent document lineage.
Operational managers review these transaction records periodically to verify adherence to organizational governance standards.

cards.title: Inspection workflow integration and return of rejected materials
cards.body:
Items flagged for mandatory inspection require formal quality verification before acceptance.
The system stops final authorization if an inspection intimation remains unresolved.
Storekeepers cannot complete receipts while technical inspection tests are pending.
Rejected quantities entered on receipt lines cannot exceed quantities rejected by inspection.
When rejected stock exists, the system enables return processing via dispatch challans.
Authorizing receipts with rejected items without creating return challans triggers warnings.
Rejected items remain isolated from usable inventory to prevent accidental operational use.
Bin card tracking requires physical storage locations for inspected stock before release.
Inspection integration ensures that substandard materials are never accepted into company stock.
Final stock authorization occurs only after quality personnel approve the delivered goods.
Returned materials generate formal debit notes to recover costs from the supplying vendor.
This quality control safeguard guarantees that only certified raw materials enter production.
Quality inspection results are permanently linked to the receipt note to ensure supplier accountability.
Rejected materials cannot be used in production or issued to internal maintenance work orders.
Operational managers review these transaction records periodically to verify adherence to organizational governance standards.
Every milestone produces an auditable record connecting original requests to final authorized financial commitments.

cards.title: Document lifecycle progression, record locking, and stock posting
cards.body:
Receipt notes advance through three formal operational statuses: Initial, Release, and Authorized.
Saving in Release status records the releaser identity and prepares the record for review.
Under multi-tier authorization, only the terminal approver can transition status to Authorized.
Attempting premature authorization produces error notifications stopping the save operation.
Final authorization is the precise event that posts physical stock into warehouse ledgers.
If the current inventory accounting month is locked, authorization is strictly prohibited.
Once authorized, the receipt note is locked against editing, number modification, or deletion.
Header and detail lines save atomically, ensuring partial updates never compromise data integrity.
Editing un-authorized receipts clears existing lines and regenerates them from current inputs.
Locked document status guarantees that historical inventory additions remain fully auditable.
Authorized receipts write permanent financial staging records consumed by purchase invoice booking.
This state progression guarantees strict segregation of duties between receiving clerks and supervisors.
Storekeepers verify that physical warehouse bin locations are ready before authorizing stock intake.
Operational managers review these transaction records periodically to verify adherence to organizational governance standards.
Every milestone produces an auditable record connecting original requests to final authorized financial commitments.

cards.title: Indent allocations, reservation balances, and status cascades
cards.body:
Receipt quantities must reconcile exactly against original departmental requisitions.
When receipts satisfy specific indents, the sum of indent allocations must equal accepted quantity.
For reserved indents, allocation amounts cannot exceed the open reserved balance.
When batch tracking or serial numbers are active, details must equal total received units.
Authorizing the receipt note automatically triggers status cascades across upstream documents.
Linked purchase orders, gate passes, and indents have their open balances decremented.
Orders with zero remaining balance are automatically updated to completed status.
Finance receives valued inward transaction records ready for purchase bill matching.
Editing an un-authorized receipt resets linked document balances before recalculating them.
These cascades keep inventory balances, procurement orders, and requisitions synchronized.
Reconciled allocations ensure that departmental requisition lines close accurately upon receipt.
Automated status cascades eliminate manual tracking of outstanding purchase order commitments.
This real-time synchronization provides management with accurate visibility of pending vendor deliveries.
Accurate indent consumption updates procurement reporting dashboards to prevent redundant purchasing.
Operational managers review these transaction records periodically to verify adherence to organizational governance standards.
Every milestone produces an auditable record connecting original requests to final authorized financial commitments.
